source: round21 telegraph assets, reopened read-only and SHA-bound; nothing re-rendered, no teacher executed, no tactical label created
features: round22.spatial_vectors reused verbatim through round23; the 94-d spatial vector it also computes is not used and only serves as the frozen proof that the encode pass is round22's

storage.dtype: uint8 (the renderer output verbatim, never cast to float on disk)
storage.container: npz deflate for the pixel regions, torch.save (xb) for history/labels
storage.scale: uint8 -> float32 /255 happens only at load through vision.regions_to_batch
storage.hud: hud_score/hud_status are byte-identical across all 80 decisions (asserted per event); stored once as [1,3,H,W,C] and expanded to 80 rows at load, so the values are identical while the 80 redundant copies are not written
storage.why: a float32 copy of the same content is 4x larger and adds nothing: every consumer divides by 255 immediately

teacher: round19 run/worlds/<family>/<event>.json, teacher_v2 action list, asserted equal to round21's stored rollout actions for all 14 train events

aux.task: from the GRU state predict whether the safe gap lies left or right OF THE PLAYER, i.e. which sign of action closes the distance to the slot: label = sign(gap screen centre - player screen x), gap from round21.telegraph_gap(s) (privileged world parameter), player x from the frozen teacher trajectory (train) or the checkpoint's own trajectory (scoring); the label is read at the first row of the telegraph window
aux.supervision_window: the rows whose logical frame 2*i lies inside round21.telegraph_window(s) = [wall_frame-45, wall_frame)
aux.reference_point: the player x, not the playfield centre 192
aux.never_an_input: the label is a training-loss target only: it is not a pixel region, not a history field, not a feature channel, and no policy head tensor depends on it

label_semantics: identical to round21 (round20 tactical labels), unchanged
